title: Monte Albán
summary: Monte Albán is the most important archaeological site of the Valley of Oaxaca, a Zapotec capital on mountain plateaus whose terraces, dams, canals, pyramids and artificial mounds were carved out of the mountain. UNESCO says it flourished for thirteen centuries from 500 BCE until its abandonment began around 850 CE. One source says it replaced San José Mogote as the valley's main settlement between 500 and 450 BCE.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says the capital flourished 'from the year 500 B.C to 850 A.D.' (500 BCE = -499); World History Encyclopedia says it replaced San José Mogote between 500 and 450 BCE and the civilization ended around 900 CE.

reviewer_note: No model: no height-plus-plan dimension for a named structure was sourced. UNESCO's XML lists two unlabelled points; I used the one matching Wikidata's Monte Albán (about 0.3 km away); the other is the Oaxaca city centre. UNESCO's text says the site was inhabited 1,500 years by Olmecs, Zapotecs and Mixtecs, while the 500 BCE-850 CE span is the Zapotec capital's flourishing.

footprint.description: South Platform closing the south end of the Gran Plaza at Monte Albán: an almost square plan of about 140 m per side, 40 m high, the highest construction of the city.

phases.description: The ceremonial esplanade bounded by two platforms was largely laid out in the Monte Albán II phase (c. 300 BC to c. 100 AD) and in Monte Albán III; the South Platform's own date is not given separately.
Platform stands in the heyday of the city, which the INAH guide says collapsed between 800 and 850 CE.
Site abandoned after the collapse; in the Postclassic a large circular wall was built in the South Platform area and used as a fortress.
